weeks.rationale: Opening week of the Nov 14 build and the week the plan gets re-anchored. The 30 Aug 10 km (3:57/km at avg HR 183) and the heart-rate half of the 11 Aug time trial together retire the 2026-06-19 lab pair: threshold is 4:16/km at ~175 bpm, not 4:34/km at 163 bpm, so every quality prescription in this block is roughly 20 s/km faster and 12-15 bpm higher than the last one. Volume steps to 66 km, the top third of the 55.8-68.2 km base band. The threshold dose is deliberately held at 4x8 min rather than pushed to 40 min: the intensity itself is the step up this week, and stacking both at once would be two progressions in one.
weeks.methodology: Polarized distribution carries the week: four of six sessions are genuinely easy volume well under the aerobic ceiling, and the three hard touches (threshold, compromised sim, long-run finish) are separated by at least one easy day. Threshold work is the shared lever for both goals - it raises LT2, which sets 21k pace and the running half of Hyrox alike - and it is anchored on measured performance rather than a percentage of max HR. Heavy compound lifting is paired onto the already-hard Tuesday so the easy days stay cleanly easy, and explosive/plyometric work sits on Friday's easy-run day, away from hard running, because same-session concurrency is where power interference actually shows up. Load progresses gradually: volume moves to the top of the band this week and the interval duration waits until the new intensity has been absorbed.

sessions.title: Upper Pull + Press (AM gym) + Easy Aerobic (PM)
sessions.prescription: AM (gym, ~55 min, FREE WEIGHTS ONLY): weighted pull-up 4x4 @ BW+5 kg; overhead press 4x4 @ 60 kg; barbell bent-over row 4x6 @ 60 kg; single-arm DB row 3x8/side @ 32 kg; DB bench press 4x5 @ 2x32 kg; bent-over DB rear-delt raise 3x12 @ 8-10 kg; farmers carry 3x40 m @ 2x32 kg. RPE 8 (~2 RIR), 2 min rest, never to failure; progress the load when a top set leaves >2 RIR. PM (home treadmill or outdoors): 59 min genuinely easy (10.0 km), HR <=145 bpm, 5:45-6:15/km, conversational. This is polarized volume - if it feels like work, slow down.
sessions.purpose: Full upper-body strength session plus the week's first block of easy aerobic volume.
sessions.why: Upper-body strength on Monday costs the legs nothing before Tuesday's threshold, which is the point of putting it here rather than on a lower-body day. The run is genuinely easy and not longer, because Tuesday is the week's first hard day and easy volume is only useful if it stays easy - stretching this to 13 km would buy 3 km at the cost of the session that matters.

sessions.title: Threshold 4x8min at the NEW anchor + Heavy Lower (double)
sessions.prescription: AM (no gym) THRESHOLD - RE-ANCHORED: 15 min easy warmup + 4 strides -> 4x8 min @ 4:20-4:10/km, HR 170-178 (NOT the old 4:34/163 - that pair is retired) with 2:30 jog recovery -> 12 min easy cooldown. Target ~4:16/km; the effort should be 'comfortably hard, could hold about an hour', not a race. PM (gym, ~55 min): back squat 4x3 @ 100 kg; trap-bar deadlift 3x3 @ 130 kg; hip thrust 3x8 @ 110 kg; walking lunge 3x20 steps @ 2x20 kg DB; weighted step-up 3x8/side @ 2x20 kg DB. RPE 8, 2-3 min rest, never to failure. No plyometrics today.

steps.target: RPE 8, ~2 RIR, 3 min rest, fast concentric

sessions.purpose: Re-set threshold at the corrected anchor and pair heavy lower onto the same hard day.
sessions.why: 32 minutes at true threshold, and the pace is the whole point: at 4:34/km you were training tempo and calling it threshold, which is why the sessions kept feeling easy. The dose stays at 4x8 rather than moving to 4x10 because raising intensity and duration in the same week is two progressions at once and there would be no way to read which one failed. Heavy lower pairs here so the week has one clean hard day instead of two compromised ones, and it goes after the run because the run is what needs fresh legs.

sessions.title: Easy Aerobic
sessions.prescription: 59 min genuinely easy (10.0 km), HR <=145 bpm, 5:45-6:15/km, conversational. This is polarized volume - if it feels like work, slow down.
sessions.purpose: Pure aerobic volume between the week's two hard days.
sessions.why: The recovery day between Tuesday's threshold and Thursday's sim, and the only job is to add kilometres without adding cost. Ten easy kilometres, not six: at 66 km/week the mid-week easy runs are where the volume actually lives, and this is the run that gets cut first when a week goes wrong - so it is prescribed in full.

sessions.title: Compromised Sim (5 rounds) - RACE PACE 4:30/km
sessions.prescription: AM (gym): 10 min easy warmup with drills and 4 strides (~1.7 km) -> 5 rounds of 1000 m at Hyrox race pace ~4:30/km (HR 165-175) straight into one station, in race order: Ski erg 1000 m; Sled push 50 m @ 202 kg; Sled pull 50 m @ 153 kg; Burpee broad jump 80 m; Wall balls x50 @ 9 kg to 3.0 m. Move to the next run immediately - the transition IS the session. 5 min jog cooldown (~0.85 km).

steps.target: strong legs, long finish, no rest into the run

sessions.purpose: Hold race pace off a station at full Men's Pro load - the quality Hyrox is decided by.
sessions.why: Race pace moves from 4:50 to 4:30/km for the same reason threshold moved: for a man who just ran 10 km at 3:57/km, 4:50 off a sled is a jog that rehearses the movement and trains nothing. Five rounds rather than six because the pace step is this week's progression and the round count is next week's. Stations stay at full competition load - specificity is the entire reason this session exists, and a lighter sled trains a race you are not entering.

sessions.title: Plyo + Economy (AM gym) + Easy Aerobic (PM)
sessions.prescription: AM (gym, ~55 min): box jump 5x3 @ 60 cm; hurdle hop 4x5; standing broad jump 4x3 (all with FULL recovery - quality, not conditioning); Romanian deadlift 3x6 @ 100 kg @ RPE 7; DB push press 3x5 @ 2x24 kg; sandbag lunge 3x50 m @ 30 kg; wall balls 3x25 @ 9 kg to 3.0 m. Keep the barbell work at RPE 7 - Saturday's long run is the priority. PM (home treadmill or outdoors): 47 min genuinely easy (8.0 km), HR <=145 bpm, 5:45-6:15/km, conversational. This is polarized volume - if it feels like work, slow down.

steps.target: RPE 7 - leave the legs for Saturday

sessions.purpose: Explosive strength for running economy, on the day it does not cost anything, plus easy volume.
sessions.why: Plyometrics live here because explosive power is the one quality concurrent training genuinely blunts, and only in the same session as hard running - on an easy-run day they are free. Barbell work is capped at RPE 7 rather than dropped: Saturday's long run needs the legs, but a 20-minute jump-only visit is not worth the trip, so the session keeps its seven movements and loses proximity to failure instead.

sessions.title: Long Run 17 km + 4x3min at 21k Pace
sessions.prescription: 70 min easy (12.0 km, HR 148-158, 5:15-5:40/km) -> 4x3 min @ 21k pace ~4:20/km (HR 168-176) with 2 min easy jog between -> 6 min easy cooldown. The reps go at the END on tired legs - that is the point.
sessions.purpose: The week's aerobic centrepiece with a race-pace finish on fatigued legs.
sessions.why: The long run is the single most transferable session for both goals and it carries a quarter of the week's volume. The finish is at 4:20/km, not 4:50, because 21k pace for a 39:35 10 km runner is roughly 4:10-4:20 - running it slower rehearses nothing you will face. Reps rather than a continuous block at this stage: the aim is to touch race pace under fatigue, not to turn Saturday into a second threshold day when Tuesday already owns that.

sessions.title: Rest
sessions.prescription: Full rest. Walk, eat, sleep. No make-up session - the week is built around this day being genuinely off.
sessions.purpose: Absorb the week's load.
sessions.why: One full rest day is what makes six training days (three of them hard) absorbable at 66+ km. Not an easy shakeout: the adaptation from Saturday's long run happens here, and a junk 6 km would cost more than the 6 km is worth.

weeks.rationale: Second base week, 9 weeks out, and the week the re-anchor gets tested rather than assumed. Tuesday's threshold session is replaced by the 30-minute time trial BENCHMARKS.md has owed since 11 August - outdoors on a flat measured loop, one even maximal effort, because the treadmill attempt failed on both counts (unpaired watch voided the pace, progressive steps voided the last-20-minute LTHR average). Volume rises to 68 km, the top of the base band, carried by the easy runs so the test has fresh legs. Everything in weeks 3 and 4 should be re-targeted to whatever this trial returns.
weeks.methodology: A time trial is a threshold session with a measurement attached, so testing costs no training - which is why the benchmark sits on the quality day rather than displacing one. Polarized structure is unchanged: easy volume dominates, three hard touches, each separated by an easy day. Gradual progression shows up as volume (66 to 68 km) and as sim rounds (five to six) rather than another intensity step, because the intensity step was last week and it needs a week to be absorbed before it is judged. Strength loads advance by the RIR rule on both gym days, and explosive work stays on the easy-run day, away from hard running.

sessions.title: Upper Pull + Press (AM gym) + Easy Aerobic (PM)
sessions.prescription: AM (gym, ~55 min): weighted pull-up 4x4 @ BW+7.5 kg; overhead press 4x4 @ 62.5 kg; barbell bent-over row 4x6 @ 62.5 kg; single-arm DB row 3x8/side @ 34 kg; DB bench press 4x6 @ 2x32 kg; rear-delt raise 3x12 @ 10 kg; farmers carry 3x50 m @ 2x32 kg. Loads stepped up from week 1 - if a top set still leaves >2 RIR, add more. PM (home treadmill or outdoors): 59 min genuinely easy (10.0 km), HR <=145 bpm, 5:45-6:15/km, conversational. This is polarized volume - if it feels like work, slow down.
sessions.purpose: Full upper-body session at stepped-up loads plus easy aerobic volume.
sessions.why: Upper body the day before a maximal running test is close to free - the legs are untouched and the aerobic cost is negligible. Loads step up 2.5 kg across the compounds because week 1's top sets are meant to have left about 2 reps in reserve; if they left more, add more. The run stays at 10 easy km rather than being trimmed 'for the test' - one easy hour does not blunt a time trial, and pre-cutting is how weeks quietly shrink.

sessions.title: 30-min TT OUTDOORS (BENCHMARK) + Heavy Lower (double)
sessions.prescription: AM (no gym) BENCHMARK - 30-MINUTE TIME TRIAL, OUTDOORS on a flat measured loop (NOT the treadmill - the 11 Aug attempt was voided by an unpaired watch). 20 min easy warmup + 4 strides (3.4 km) -> 30 min ALL-OUT AS ONE EVEN EFFORT (~7.15 km at ~4:12/km if the re-anchor is right). Do NOT step the pace up through the test: even splits, at most a small negative finish. Record the average HR of the LAST 20 MINUTES - that is LTHR - and the total distance, which gives threshold pace. -> 20 min easy cooldown (3.4 km). PM (gym, ~55 min): back squat 4x3 @ 102.5 kg; trap-bar deadlift 4x3 @ 132.5 kg; hip thrust 3x8 @ 115 kg; walking lunge 3x24 @ 2x20 kg DB; weighted step-up 3x8/side @ 2x22 kg DB. If the trial emptied you, cut to 3 sets per lift - do not skip the session.

steps.target: ~4:12/km if the re-anchor holds; log last-20-min avg HR = LTHR
log both in BENCHMARKS.md the same day
RPE 8, 3 min rest - cut to 3 sets if the TT emptied you

sessions.purpose: Measure LTHR and threshold pace directly, replacing an inferred anchor with a tested one.
sessions.why: The whole block currently rests on a threshold inferred from a 10 km race and a botched treadmill trial; one clean 30-minute effort replaces that inference with a measurement, and it is the retest BENCHMARKS.md already specifies. It costs no training because a 30-minute maximal effort IS a threshold session - a slightly bigger one than 4x8. Outdoors and even-paced are non-negotiable: an unpaired watch voids the pace and progressive steps void the LTHR average, which is exactly how the last attempt was lost. Heavy lower still runs afterwards - it is downstream of the test and cutting sets is the right lever if the trial hurt, not cancelling.

sessions.title: Easy Aerobic
sessions.prescription: 59 min genuinely easy (10.0 km), HR <=145 bpm, 5:45-6:15/km, conversational. This is polarized volume - if it feels like work, slow down.
sessions.purpose: Aerobic volume and recovery from the time trial.
sessions.why: The day after a maximal effort, and deliberately still 10 km: easy running the day after hard work clears more than sitting does, provided it is genuinely easy. Cap it at the easy HR ceiling and let the pace be whatever that allows - if that means 6:20/km today, that is the correct pace, not a failure.

sessions.title: Compromised Sim (6 rounds) - RACE PACE 4:30/km
sessions.prescription: AM (gym): 10 min easy warmup with drills (~1.7 km) -> 6 rounds of 1000 m at Hyrox race pace ~4:30/km (HR 165-175) straight into one station, in race order: Ski erg 1000 m; Sled push 50 m @ 202 kg; Sled pull 50 m @ 153 kg; Burpee broad jump 80 m; Farmers carry 200 m @ 2x32 kg; Wall balls x50 @ 9 kg. No rest at the transitions. 5 min jog cooldown (~0.85 km).
sessions.purpose: Six rounds of race-pace running off full-load stations - the week's second hard day.
sessions.why: Six rounds now that 4:30/km has had a week: the round count is this week's progression, held back last week so the pace step could be judged on its own. Farmers carry enters the rotation because grip and trunk fatigue is what actually costs pace on the run after it. Pace is held at 4:30 rather than pushed - going faster here would turn a race-specific session into a second threshold day two days after a time trial, and the week already has its quality.

sessions.title: Plyo + Economy (AM gym) + Easy Aerobic (PM)
sessions.prescription: AM (gym, ~55 min): box jump 5x3 @ 65 cm; hurdle hop 4x5; standing broad jump 4x3 (full recovery throughout); Romanian deadlift 3x6 @ 105 kg @ RPE 7; DB push press 3x5 @ 2x26 kg; sandbag lunge 3x50 m @ 30 kg; wall balls 3x30 @ 9 kg. PM (home treadmill or outdoors): 47 min genuinely easy (8.0 km), HR <=145 bpm, 5:45-6:15/km, conversational. This is polarized volume - if it feels like work, slow down.
sessions.purpose: Explosive work for economy plus easy volume, on the day it costs nothing.
sessions.why: Box height and push-press load step up while the jump volume stays low - plyometric progression is quality per contact, not more contacts, and adding sets here would make it conditioning and cost Saturday. RDL climbs to 105 kg but stays at RPE 7 for the same reason. The easy run holds at 8 km so the week's volume lands on Saturday, where it does the most for the 21k.

sessions.title: Long Run 17.5 km + 5x3min at 21k Pace
sessions.prescription: 68 min easy (11.65 km, HR 148-158, 5:15-5:40/km) -> 5x3 min @ 21k pace ~4:18/km (HR 168-176) with 2 min easy jog between -> 6 min easy cooldown. Re-target the rep pace to Tuesday's TT result if it moved.
sessions.purpose: Largest base-week long run with a fifth rep added to the race-pace finish.
sessions.why: 17.5 km is the week's volume anchor and the fifth rep is a small, honest step from four - progression by one repetition is readable, progression by three is not. The reps stay at the end on tired legs because 21k performance is decided by what pace survives at 17 km, not what pace is available at 3 km. Not extended past 17.5 km this week: the time trial was Tuesday, and the long run is where accumulated fatigue shows up last and hurts most.

sessions.title: Rest
sessions.prescription: Full rest. Walk, eat, sleep. No make-up session - the week is built around this day being genuinely off.
sessions.purpose: Absorb the week's load.
sessions.why: One full rest day is what makes six training days (three of them hard) absorbable at 66+ km. Not an easy shakeout: the adaptation from Saturday's long run happens here, and a junk 6 km would cost more than the 6 km is worth.

weeks.rationale: First BUILD week and the peak of this block, 8 weeks out. Volume reaches 71 km - the top of the 58.6-71.6 km build band and the highest week of the macrocycle so far - and the threshold dose finally steps to 4x10 min (40 min) now that the corrected intensity has had two weeks to settle. The sim rotates to rowing, sandbag lunges and 75 wall balls, the movements the last two weeks skipped. Every pace here should be re-targeted to the week-2 time trial rather than the numbers written below, if the trial moved them.
weeks.methodology: Build phase raises race-specific work without abandoning the polarized base: the easy runs still carry most of the volume, and the three hard days remain separated. Threshold progresses by interval duration, not by pace - once the anchor is correct, running faster leaves LT2 instead of training it, while more time at it raises the ceiling. Strength adds a set on the heavy lifts rather than load on every lift, the least disruptive way to progress alongside a volume peak. Plyometrics stay on the easy-run day and away from hard running. This is the week the block's progression is judged on: if it lands, the ramp is working; if it does not, that is the signal to hold rather than push into October.

sessions.title: Upper Pull + Press (AM gym) + Easy Aerobic (PM)
sessions.prescription: AM (gym, ~60 min): weighted pull-up 5x4 @ BW+7.5 kg; overhead press 4x3 @ 65 kg; barbell bent-over row 4x6 @ 65 kg; single-arm DB row 3x8/side @ 34 kg; DB bench press 5x5 @ 2x34 kg (2x32 for 6-8 if 34s are unavailable); rear-delt raise 3x12 @ 10 kg; farmers carry 3x60 m @ 2x32 kg. PM (home treadmill or outdoors): 62 min genuinely easy (10.5 km), HR <=145 bpm, 5:45-6:15/km, conversational. This is polarized volume - if it feels like work, slow down.
sessions.purpose: Highest-volume upper session of the block plus easy aerobic volume.
sessions.why: Pull-ups and bench each gain a set rather than jumping load again - in the block's highest-volume running week, adding sets is the cheaper progression, because the extra fatigue is local and does not follow you into Tuesday. The run grows to 10.5 km as part of the volume peak; it is upper-body day precisely so the extra kilometres cost nothing before the week's biggest threshold session.

sessions.title: Threshold 4x10min + Heavy Lower (double)
sessions.prescription: AM (no gym) THRESHOLD: 15 min easy warmup + 4 strides -> 4x10 min @ threshold (4:20-4:10/km, HR 170-178 - RE-TARGET to the week-2 TT result) with 2:30 jog recovery -> 10 min easy cooldown. 40 minutes of work, the block's largest dose. PM (gym, ~60 min): back squat 5x3 @ 105 kg; trap-bar deadlift 4x3 @ 135 kg; hip thrust 4x8 @ 115 kg; walking lunge 3x24 @ 2x22 kg DB; weighted step-up 4x8/side @ 2x22 kg DB. RPE 8, never to failure. No plyometrics today.
sessions.purpose: The block's largest threshold dose plus its heaviest lower session, on one clean hard day.
sessions.why: 40 minutes at true threshold is the single most valuable session in the block for both goals, and it is reachable now only because weeks 1 and 2 established that the corrected pace is sustainable. Progressed by duration and not pace: past LT2 the session becomes VO2 work, which is a different adaptation and a much more expensive one this far out. Heavy lower pairs here again to keep the week to three hard days; it is the heaviest lift of the block, and it goes second because the run is what the week is built around.

sessions.title: Easy Aerobic
sessions.prescription: 62 min genuinely easy (10.5 km), HR <=145 bpm, 5:45-6:15/km, conversational. This is polarized volume - if it feels like work, slow down.
sessions.purpose: The volume peak's mid-week aerobic block.
sessions.why: 10.5 easy kilometres between the two hardest days of the block. In a 71 km week the temptation is to trim here, but this run is pure aerobic return at almost no cost - the expensive sessions are Tuesday and Thursday, and they are unchanged. Keep it under the easy ceiling; the entire point is that it is not a third quality day.

sessions.title: Compromised Sim (6 rounds) - RACE PACE 4:25/km
sessions.prescription: AM (gym): 10 min easy warmup with drills (~1.7 km) -> 6 rounds of 1000 m at ~4:25/km (HR 165-175) straight into one station: Rowing 1000 m; Sled push 50 m @ 202 kg; Sled pull 50 m @ 153 kg; Sandbag lunge 100 m @ 30 kg; Farmers carry 200 m @ 2x32 kg; Wall balls x75 @ 9 kg. No rest at the transitions. 8 min jog cooldown (~1.3 km).
sessions.purpose: Race pace off the stations that hurt most, with the wall-ball set stretched toward race length.
sessions.why: Pace steps to 4:25/km and the wall balls to 75 because the two stations that decide a Hyrox - the sandbag lunge and the final 100 wall balls - are the ones least rehearsed so far, and the run after them is where the race is lost. Rowing replaces the ski erg to cover the other machine. Still 75 reps rather than the full 100: that comes in the taper block, when there is no 71 km week underneath it and the set can be done at genuine race quality.

sessions.title: Plyo + Economy (AM gym) + Easy Aerobic (PM)
sessions.prescription: AM (gym, ~60 min): box jump 6x3 @ 65 cm; hurdle hop 5x5; standing broad jump 4x3; Romanian deadlift 4x6 @ 105 kg @ RPE 7; DB push press 3x5 @ 2x26 kg; sandbag lunge 4x50 m @ 30 kg; wall balls 3x33 @ 9 kg. PM (home treadmill or outdoors): 47 min genuinely easy (8.0 km), HR <=145 bpm, 5:45-6:15/km, conversational. This is polarized volume - if it feels like work, slow down.
sessions.purpose: Peak-week explosive session plus easy volume before the longest run of the block.
sessions.why: The one session that grows in the block's hardest week is the cheapest one - jumps and RDLs at RPE 7 cost almost nothing systemically while doing real work for running economy. The run stays at 8 km deliberately: Saturday is 18 km and the week is already at its ceiling, so the extra kilometres belong there, where they train the 21k, not here.

sessions.title: Long Run 18 km + 6x3min at 21k Pace
sessions.prescription: 68 min easy (11.65 km, HR 148-158) -> 6x3 min @ 21k pace ~4:16/km (HR 168-176) with 2 min easy jog between -> 3 min easy cooldown. 18 minutes at race pace starting at km 12 - the hardest long run of the block.
sessions.purpose: Longest run of the block with 18 minutes of race pace accumulated on tired legs.
sessions.why: Six reps at 4:16/km from km 12 onward is the closest this block gets to 21k specificity, and it is the session that most directly transfers to the running half of Hyrox as well. Reps rather than a continuous 6 km block because the jog recoveries let the pace stay honest at 4:16 - a continuous block at km 12 would drift to 4:35 and become tempo. The cooldown is short by design: the reps are the point and the week is finished after them.

sessions.title: Rest
sessions.prescription: Full rest. Walk, eat, sleep. No make-up session - the week is built around this day being genuinely off.
sessions.purpose: Absorb the week's load.
sessions.why: One full rest day is what makes six training days (three of them hard) absorbable at 66+ km. Not an easy shakeout: the adaptation from Saturday's long run happens here, and a junk 6 km would cost more than the 6 km is worth.

weeks.rationale: Absorb week, 7 weeks out, closing the block. Volume drops to 64 km from 71 and the strength work drops a set at RPE 7, but the intensity is untouched: threshold returns to 4x8 min at full pace, the sim runs four rounds at 4:25/km, and Saturday keeps a continuous 5 km at Hyrox race pace. Nothing is deleted - every session survives at a lower dose. This week exists so the next block can open on absorbed fitness rather than accumulated fatigue, with 6 weeks left to build into the taper.
weeks.methodology: Cutting volume while holding intensity is the well-supported way to absorb a load block - the same principle that governs a race taper, applied at a smaller scale. The polarized shape and the day structure are unchanged so the week is directly comparable to the three before it. Strength keeps every movement and drops a set and one RPE point rather than shortening into an add-on, since a gym visit is a fixed cost either way. Saturday swaps intervals for a continuous 5 km at race pace: with less fatigue underneath it, a continuous block can be held honestly, which is a better read on where 21k fitness actually sits going into October.

sessions.title: Upper Pull + Press (AM gym) + Easy Aerobic (PM)
sessions.prescription: AM (gym, ~45 min) ABSORB WEEK - same movements, one set fewer and RPE 7 (3 RIR), loads back to week-1 numbers: weighted pull-up 3x4 @ BW+5 kg; overhead press 3x4 @ 60 kg; barbell bent-over row 3x6 @ 60 kg; single-arm DB row 3x8/side @ 32 kg; DB bench press 3x6 @ 2x32 kg; rear-delt raise 3x12 @ 8 kg; farmers carry 2x50 m @ 2x32 kg. PM (home treadmill or outdoors): 53 min genuinely easy (9.0 km), HR <=145 bpm, 5:45-6:15/km, conversational. This is polarized volume - if it feels like work, slow down.
sessions.purpose: Reduced-dose upper session plus easy aerobic volume.
sessions.why: Same seven movements, one set fewer, RPE 7 instead of 8, week-1 loads - the trip is still worth making and nothing is lost from the pattern, only from the fatigue. The run comes down to 9 km as part of the absorb; cutting the easy runs is the right place to take volume out, because the quality sessions are what the week is protecting.

sessions.title: Threshold 4x8min (full pace, reduced dose) + Lower (double)
sessions.prescription: AM (no gym) THRESHOLD: 15 min easy warmup + 4 strides -> 4x8 min @ threshold (4:20-4:10/km, HR 170-178 - use the week-2 TT numbers) with 2:30 jog recovery -> 10 min easy cooldown. 32 min of work, down from 40, at the SAME pace. PM (gym, ~45 min): back squat 3x3 @ 100 kg; trap-bar deadlift 3x3 @ 130 kg; hip thrust 3x6 @ 110 kg; walking lunge 2x20 @ 2x20 kg DB; weighted step-up 3x8/side @ 2x20 kg DB. All at RPE 7 (3 RIR).
sessions.purpose: Hold threshold pace at a reduced dose so the intensity is maintained while fatigue clears.
sessions.why: Volume comes off, pace does not - dropping the pace as well would let the adaptation of the last three weeks decay, which is the opposite of what an absorb week is for. 32 minutes at threshold is still a real session, just 8 minutes shorter than last week. Heavy lower keeps all five movements at RPE 7: the trade-off here is proximity to failure, not the trip to the gym.

sessions.title: Easy Aerobic
sessions.prescription: 56 min genuinely easy (9.5 km), HR <=145 bpm, 5:45-6:15/km, conversational. This is polarized volume - if it feels like work, slow down.
sessions.purpose: Mid-week aerobic volume at the absorb-week dose.
sessions.why: 9.5 km rather than 10.5 - the absorb comes out of the easy runs first, because they are the most fungible kilometres in the week. Still a real run and not a shakeout: the aerobic base is the thing being preserved, and 'absorb' means less load, not less training.

sessions.title: Compromised Sim (4 rounds) - RACE PACE 4:25/km
sessions.prescription: AM (gym): 10 min easy warmup with drills (~1.7 km) -> 4 rounds of 1000 m at ~4:25/km (HR 165-175) straight into one station: Ski erg 1000 m; Sled push 50 m @ 202 kg; Sandbag lunge 100 m @ 30 kg; Wall balls x100 @ 9 kg (the FULL race set, in sets of 25). No rest at the transitions. 10 min jog cooldown (~1.7 km).

steps.target: FULL race set, to 3.0 m, sets of 25

sessions.purpose: Fewer rounds at full pace, finishing with the complete 100-rep wall-ball set.
sessions.why: Four rounds instead of six is where the absorb is taken, and it buys the freshness to do the one thing this session has never done: the full 100 wall balls, at race load, after three rounds of compromised running. That set is the most common place a Hyrox falls apart and it needs to be rehearsed intact at least once per block. Pace holds at 4:25 - the reduction is in quantity, not quality.

sessions.title: Plyo + Economy (AM gym) + Easy Aerobic (PM)
sessions.prescription: AM (gym, ~45 min): box jump 4x3 @ 60 cm; hurdle hop 3x5; standing broad jump 3x3; Romanian deadlift 3x6 @ 100 kg @ RPE 7; DB push press 3x5 @ 2x24 kg; sandbag lunge 2x50 m @ 30 kg; wall balls 3x25 @ 9 kg. PM (home treadmill or outdoors): 41 min genuinely easy (7.0 km), HR <=145 bpm, 5:45-6:15/km, conversational. This is polarized volume - if it feels like work, slow down.
sessions.purpose: Reduced-volume explosive session plus easy volume before Saturday's race-pace run.
sessions.why: Jump volume drops by roughly a third while the intent stays maximal - explosive work responds to freshness, so an absorb week is when it is done best, not skipped. The run is the shortest of the week at 7 km because Saturday carries a continuous 5 km at race pace and that is where the week's remaining quality belongs.

sessions.title: Long Run 18 km with a continuous 5 km at Race Pace
sessions.prescription: 65 min easy (11.15 km, HR 148-158) -> 5 km CONTINUOUS at ~4:25/km (22 min, HR 168-176), no breaks -> 10 min easy cooldown (1.7 km). One unbroken block, not reps - hold the pace or finish the block slower, but do not stop.
sessions.purpose: A continuous race-pace block on tired legs - the block's closing read on 21k and Hyrox running fitness.
sessions.why: The absorb week is the only week with enough freshness underneath it to hold 5 km unbroken at 4:25/km from km 11, which makes it the honest test of whether the block worked - and unlike a time trial, it costs nothing extra because it replaces the interval finish rather than adding to it. Continuous rather than reps on purpose: what both races demand is pace that does not decay, and jog recoveries hide decay. The volume around it is cut, not the block itself.

sessions.title: Rest
sessions.prescription: Full rest. Walk, eat, sleep. No make-up session - the week is built around this day being genuinely off.
sessions.purpose: Absorb the week's load.
sessions.why: One full rest day is what makes six training days (three of them hard) absorbable at 66+ km. Not an easy shakeout: the adaptation from Saturday's long run happens here, and a junk 6 km would cost more than the 6 km is worth.
